Definition: to lift, in a great variety of applications, literal and figurative, absolute and relative
BiblicalUsage: 1) to lift, bear up, carry, take; 1a) (Qal); 1a1) to lift, lift up; 1a2) to bear, carry, support, sustain, endure; 1a3) to take, take away, carry off, forgive; 1b) (Niphal); 1b1) to be lifted up, be exalted; 1b2) to lift oneself up, rise up; 1b3) to be borne, be carried; 1b4) to be taken away, be carried off, be swept away; 1c) (Piel); 1c1) to lift up, exalt, support, aid, assist; 1c2) to desire, long (fig.); 1c3) to carry, bear continuously; 1c4) to take, take away; 1d) (Hithpael) to lift oneself up, exalt oneself; 1e) (Hiphil); 1e1) to cause one to bear (iniquity); 1e2) to cause to bring, have brought
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
